==Biography==
==={{BotW|-}}===
{{Quests|
{{BotW Quest
 |name= Divine Beast Vah Medoh (Quest)
 |image= Divine Beast Vah Medoh
 |display= Divine Beast Vah Medoh
 |type= Main Quest

Teba is the most skilled [[Rito]] warrior in [[Rito Village]].<ref name="CaC 128"/> He resides in his [[Teba's Home|Home]] with his wife [[Saki]] and his son [[Tulin]]. Teba is known to be prideful to the point of recklessness, and Saki describes him as impulsive.<ref name="CaC 128"/><ref name="BotW Saki"/> Like other Rito warriors, Teba idolizes [[Revali]], and he wishes for Tulin to become a great warrior as well.<ref name="BotW Saki 2"/><ref name="BotW Kaneli 2"/>

Growing up, Teba was childhood friends with [[Harth]].<ref name="CaC 400"/> Since Tulin is close in age with Harth's daughter, [[Molli]], their families have remained close.<ref name="BotW Harth"/> Teba was also mentored by [[Kaneli]] while training to become a Rito warrior.<ref name="CaC 400"/> When [[Divine Beast Vah Medoh]] reactivated and began circling Rito Village, Teba and Harth went to face it, ignoring Kaneli's warnings.<ref name="BotW Kaneli 3"/> This resulted in Harth becoming injured, though Teba remained unscathed.<ref name="BotW Kaneli 3"/>

[[File:BotW Teba Introduction.png|thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Teba repairing a Falcon Bow at the Flight Range. Text on-screen displays his name, along with the title "Rito Warrior".|Teba's introduction]]
When [[Link]] speaks to Saki during the "[[Divine Beast Vah Medoh (Quest)|Divine Beast Vah Medoh]]" [[Main Quest]], she reveals that Teba is absent from the Village, as he is preparing for another attack on Vah Medoh at the [[Flight Range]].<ref name="BotW Saki 3"/> At the Flight Range, Link can find Teba working on a [[Falcon Bow]]. He turns to face Link when he senses his approach.<ref name="BotW Teba 2"/> Realizing he does not know Link, Teba tells him to leave since he is busy.<ref name="BotW Teba 3"/>

Upon speaking to Teba, he reiterates that he is busy and asks Link if he needs something.<ref name="BotW Teba 4"/> If Link claims that he can help him, Teba initially does not know what he is talking about.<ref name="BotW Teba 5"/> When Link clarifies that he can calm Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba is skeptical that of his story, and he asks Link for his name.<ref name="BotW Teba 6"/> After they introduce themselves to each other, Teba voices his suspicions that Kaneli had Link come to talk him out of facing Vah Medoh.<ref name="BotW Teba 7"/> When Link confirms this, Teba is annoyed, but asserts that he will not return to Rito Village until he defeats the [[Divine Beast]].<ref name="BotW Teba 7"/><ref name="BotW Teba 8"/>

After Link reasserts his desire to help, Teba states that he is in no position to talk him out of it.<ref name="BotW Teba 9"/> He recalls Kaneli saying that the only way to stop Divine Beast Vah Medoh would be to enter it, which he believes to be impossible.<ref name="BotW Teba 9"/> Though Link tries to tell him that he is capable of doing so, Teba does not believe him, since only the [[Champions]] would be capable of entering a Divine Beast.<ref name="BotW Teba 10"/>

Teba decides to instead focus on fighting Divine Beast Vah Medoh.<ref name="BotW Teba 10"/> He explains that if they approach the Divine Beast without a plan, they will be shot down by its [[Cannon (Enemy)|Cannons]].<ref name="BotW Teba 10"/> Therefore, he wants to test Link's skills before they attempt their assault.<ref name="BotW Teba 10"/> To do so, Link must use the Flight Range's [[Updraft]]s to destroy five [[Target]]s within three minutes.<ref name="BotW Teba 11"/> If Link asks for a tip, Teba explains that using a [[Bow]] in midair is the same as using it on the ground.<ref name="BotW Teba 12"/> He also suggests that Link use a Bow with a long range.<ref name="BotW Teba 12"/> He states that if Link is unable to complete this task, then he will not fare well against Divine Beast Vah Medoh.<ref name="BotW Teba 12"/> Once Link tells Teba he is ready, the [[Flight Range (Mini-Game)|Flight Range]] [[Mini-Game]] begins.<ref name="BotW Teba 13"/>

After Link destroys five Targets, Teba calls him back to the Flight Range's hut.<ref name="BotW Teba 14"/> Teba is impressed by Link's skills with a bow, and he confesses that he thought someone was pulling a prank on him when Link first came to the Flight Range.<ref name="BotW Teba 15"/> However, he can now tell that Link is serious about helping him, reasoning he must have seen at least a couple of battles.<ref name="BotW Teba 15"/> If Link claims to have seen a few, Teba tells him not to be modest.<ref name="BotW Teba 16"/> He remarks that he feels like he has heard the name "Link" before.<ref name="BotW Teba 17"/>

Confident in Link's abilities, Teba decides it is time for them to face Divine Beast Vah Medoh.<ref name="BotW Teba 17"/> Teba explains that he will help Link get into position so that he can shoot at the Cannons.<ref name="BotW Teba 17"/> To this end, he allows Link to take a spare Falcon Bow he modified from the nearby [[Treasure Chest]].<ref name="BotW Teba 17"/> After Link takes the Bow, Teba gives him a bundle of 20 [[Bomb Arrow]]s to use against the Divine Beast.<ref name="BotW Teba 18"/> Since they will be in a [[Freezing Climate]], Teba also suggests that Link should bring warm [[Food]] or [[Armor]].<ref name="BotW Teba 19"/>

When Link tells Teba he is ready, he first wants to know why Link is risking so much to face the Divine Beast.<ref name="BotW Teba 20"/> If Link responds that he intends to rescue [[Princess Zelda|Zelda]], Teba becomes confused and questions her relation to this matter.<ref name="BotW Teba 21"/> So long as Link is helping him, however, he does not care.<ref name="BotW Teba 21"/> He tells Link to get on his back, and the pair flies up to Divine Beast Vah Medoh.<ref name="BotW Teba 22"/>
[[File:BotW Link Riding Teba.png|thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Teba flying with Link riding on his back.|Teba flying with Link]]
As they approach Vah Medoh, Teba remarks that even he feels cold.<ref name="BotW Teba 23"/> He then points out the Divine Beast, becoming annoyed that it has restored its [[Medoh's Barrier|Barrier]].<ref name="BotW Teba 24"/> Teba goes over their plan once more, reiterating that it is Link's job to shoot the Cannons while he draws their fire.<ref name="BotW Teba 25"/> Should Link need to stop the fight, Teba tells him to [[Paraglider|Paraglide]] directly upward.<ref name="BotW Teba 25"/> In addition, he reveals that Medoh's Barrier in impenetrable and should not be touched.<ref name="BotW Teba 25"/> He also makes sure that Link remembers his [[Cold Resistance]].<ref name="BotW Teba 25"/> He tells Link that they will move when he is ready.<ref name="BotW Teba 26"/>

During the battle with Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba encourages Link.<ref name="BotW Teba 27"/> He also warns Link of incoming attacks from a Cannon.<ref name="BotW Teba 28"/><ref name="BotW Teba 29"/> Whenever Link destroys a Cannon, Teba cheers for him.<ref name="BotW Teba 30"/><ref name="BotW Teba 31"/><ref name="BotW Teba 32"/><ref name="BotW Teba 34"/>

With all of the Cannons destroyed, Teba commends Link for his work.<ref name="BotW Teba 35"/> He suddenly falters, however, as he has a burn mark on his left leg. Teba informs Link of his injury and that he plans to return to the Flight Range.<ref name="BotW Teba 36"/> However, he is concerned that he may not be able to make it back.<ref name="BotW Teba 37"/> He tells Link to continue on to Divine Beast Vah Medoh, wishing him luck as he gives him a thumbs up.<ref name="BotW Teba 38"/> Teba then descends back to the Flight Range.

If Link exits Divine Beast Vah Medoh before activating its [[Main Control Unit]], Teba can be found sitting at the Flight Range, groaning in pain over his injured leg.<ref name="BotW Teba 39"/> He is angered that he was shot, and he admits that his injury is worse than he thought.<ref name="BotW Teba 40"/> Teba curses, angered that he was forced to turn back after getting so close to defeating the Divine Beast.<ref name="BotW Teba 40"/>

Once Vah Medoh has been calmed, Teba returns to his Home in Rito Village. There, Saki tends to his wounds, and he recovers enough to be able to stand.<ref name="BotW Teba 41"/> According to Saki, Teba told her about his and Link's actions, as well as the fact that they saved Rito Village.<ref name="BotW Saki 4"/> Teba also explains that Saki told him that that Link is a descendant of the [[Hylian]] Champion, but when Link tries to tell him the truth, Teba does not believe him.<ref name="BotW Teba 41"/><ref name="BotW Teba 42"/>

After the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest has been completed, Teba admits that he would not have been able to face the Divine Beast without Link and thanks him.<ref name="BotW Teba 43"/> Once Link has the [[Great Eagle Bow]], Teba notices that he is carrying it.<ref name="BotW Teba 44"/> He admits that the Bow is too heavy for him to carry, as he would end up losing speed whenever he tried to take a shot.<ref name="BotW Teba 44"/> When he saw Link's skills with a Bow, he told Kaneli that they should give it to Link.<ref name="BotW Teba 44"/>
[[File:BotW Teba Carrying Tulin.png|thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Teba flying away from Rito Village, with Tulin riding on his back.|Teba and Tulin flying together]]
Now that his injuries are mostly healed, Teba decides to resume training Tulin at the Flight Range, expressing his hope for his son to become as great a warrior as Revali was.<ref name="BotW Teba 45"/> When Link tells him to take care, Teba stands and announces they are leaving,<ref name="BotW Teba 46"/> much to Tulin's excitement.<ref name="BotW Tulin"/> Seeing his son's happiness, Teba laughs.<ref name="BotW Teba 47"/> He then informs Link that he will be at the Flight Range for the foreseeable future.<ref name="BotW Teba 48"/> With Tulin riding on his back, Teba then departs for the Flight Range. 

Afterward, anytime Link speaks to Teba at the Flight Range, he asks if he could demonstrate his archery skills for Tulin, since he believes it could be beneficial to his training.<ref name="BotW Teba 49"/>

When {{TCB}} [[Downloadable Content]] Pack is active, ''[[The Diary of Revali]]'' appears in Teba's Home, having been entrusted to him by Kaneli.<ref name="BotW Kaneli"/> Link is also able to ask Teba about Revali, who reveals that Revali was the first Rito to be able to ascend into the air on his own without the help of [[Wind]].<ref name="BotW Teba 50"/> While Teba is currently unable to do so, he aspires to teach himself and master [[Revali's Gale]].<ref name="BotW Teba 50"/> In addition, Link is able to ask about Kaneli's whereabout, who Teba thinks is in his [[Kaneli's House|House]] in Rito Village.<ref name="BotW Teba 51"/> He hopes that Kaneli could teach Tulin some of the stories he knows about Revali, but he believes that his son's training should come first.<ref name="BotW Teba 51"/>

==Other Appearances==
==={{AoC|-}}===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
[[File:AoC Teba Introduction.png|thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Teba posing as the text, "Teba, Rito Warrior" appears.|Teba's introduction]]
Teba first appears in the [[Scenario]], [[Air and Lightning]], where [[Revali]] is battling against [[Windblight Ganon]] around [[Divine Beast Vah Medoh]]. As Revali falters against Windblight Ganon, Teba is summoned through [[Terrako]]'s [[Gate of Time]], and he uses his [[Falcon Bow]] to shoot [[Arrow]]s at Windblight Ganon's cannon.

By the time the [[Warrior]]s are able to enter Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba has teamed up with Revali by dodging Windblight's attacks to distract it. He calls out to Revali, who lets loose three [[Bomb Arrow]]s as revenge.<ref name="AoC Teba"/> Windblight Ganon uses its cannon to shoot a powerful gust to deflect the Arrows, frustrating Teba.<ref name="AoC Teba 2"/> Revali reassures Teba, as he notices that they have bought enough time for the party to board Vah Medoh to help.<ref name="AoC Revali"/>

Once Windblight Ganon retreats, the Warriors convenes on top of Divine Beast Vah Medoh. [[Urbosa]] and takes a moment to thank the party and [[Riju]] for coming to their aid. Teba, upon witnessing Revali's insincere gratitude towards [[Link]] rescuing him, is surprised by his demeanor.<ref name="AoC Revali 2"/> However, his musing is interrupted by Urbosa, who asks [[Zelda]] what happened at [[Hyrule Castle]].<ref name="AoC Urbosa"/>

After hearing these recent events, Teba joins Revali to help him defend [[Western Hyrule]] from a surge of monsters and corrupted [[Guardian]]s. During the [[Movie]] "[[Vah Medoh's Pilots]]", Teba defends Revali from [[Guardian Skywatcher]]s as he pilots the [[Divine Beast]]. When the Skywatchers persue him, Revali returns the favor by hitting his pursuers, causing Teba to be impressed by Revali's skill.<ref name="AoC Teba 3"/> With confidence, Revali boasts about showcasing Vah Medoh's power.<ref name="AoC Revali 3"/> As they take out numerous Monster outposts, Windblight Ganon reappears a few times in a final attempt to kill both Teba and Revali, but Revali is able to finally slay the demon.

In the {{GoR}} [[Downloadable Content]] Scenario, "[[EX Searching Hyrule Forest]]", Revali notices an unfamiliar Rito child disappear in [[Korok Forest]]. He reports to Teba that he saw a Rito child with the same colored feathers as Teba.<ref name="AoC Teba 4"/> Horrified, Teba pleads to tag along with Revali and two [[Rito Captain]]s, to which Revali agrees to. In Korok Forest, Teba asks for a further description of the missing child, with Revali replying that the child's face is a bit similar to Teba's.<ref name="AoC Revali 4"/>

After some searching, Teba discovers that the child is his son, [[Tulin]], and is grateful that he is safe.<ref name="AoC Teba 5"/> Tulin explains that he somehow ended up in the forest and he was looked after by "[[Korok|tiny creatures]]", which intrigues his father.<ref name="AoC Tulin"/> Teba is uncomfortable leaving Tulin alone in the forest, and a Rito Captain volunteers to protect Tulin on their way out.

While exiting the Forest, Teba introduces Tulin to Revali, who is pleasantly surprised that they are related and both have traveled through time. Tulin praises Revali, but mistakenly believes that he is just another Rito warrior who might be just as good as the Rito Champion, which a shocked Revali corrects him that he is actually the real deal. During their journey out, Tulin continues to be amazed by Revali's prowess, leading him to believe that he is still worshipped even after a hundred years. When they make it to their destination, which turned out to be a dead end, Revali becomes flustered that they should have consulted the help from the Koroks, but Tulin who can read the wind and was given knowledge on the false passages, reveals the way out and after revealing the second passage, Revali becomes impressed by Tulin's skills in understanding the wind as the child guides the grownups out. After a final surge of monsters, Teba thanks Revali for his help, but Revali tells him to stop with the excessive praise.

Once they are able to escape to the forest entrance, Teba lets Tulin off his back and reminds Tulin to use his manners since Revali was the reason he was found.<ref name="AoC Teba 6"/> Tulin complies as he trots to stand in front of the Rito Champion and gives him his gratitude.<ref name="AoC Tulin 2"/><ref name="AoC Tulin 3"/> Revali smiles a bit and compliments him back.<ref name="AoC Revali 5"/> Overjoyed to hear this,<ref name="AoC Tulin 4"/> Tulin lets him know of his intentions to train so that he can be like him as he jumped close to Revali's face as he nervously backs away, and adds that he also will one day master the Great Eagle Bow.<ref name="AoC Tulin 5"/> Revali sighs as he reminds him that he could have been killed by the monsters in the forest and notes that he wasn't the least bit scared.<ref name="AoC Revali 6"/> He looks over at Teba and notes that Tulin will eventually master the wind.<ref name="AoC Revali 7"/> Teba agrees, but he adds that he must surpass his father first.<ref name="AoC Teba 7"/> Tulin then imitates Revali's speaking patterns,<ref name="AoC Tulin 6"/> prompting a laugh from Teba before he stops himself upon seeing Revali's resigned face.<ref name="AoC Revali 8"/> Teba struggled to find the right words, but then Revali succumbs into a warm laughing fit.<ref name="AoC Revali 9"/> as Teba and Tulin soon follow. Tulin then attempts his own version of Revali's Gale, which he calls "Tulin's Tornado" only to fall on his back,<ref name="AoC Tulin 7"/> as Teba walks up to him,<ref name="AoC Teba 8"/> as Revali chuckles and reminds Tulin that he still has to keep at it.<ref name="AoC Revali 10"/>

In the "[[All Hyrule, United]]" Scenario, Purah had managed to get the Sheikah Towers back in working condition and supercharges it to bring armies of all races together, including the Champions, Divine Beasts, and the reformed Yiga Clan. Revali, noticeably more relaxed and light-hearted than he initially was, is fully content with flaunting their power as a whole,<ref name="AoC Revali 11"/> and Teba encourages Revali to make his people proud of him.<ref name="AoC Teba 9"/> With her surviving father's approval, Princess Zelda takes command of the united army and gives a powerful speech charging for the outposts and taking out the monsters that uphold the barrier so that the Champion Pilots can open fire upon Calamity Ganon. Despite the monster reviving Blood Moon holding them back, the army managed to move forward.

In "[[The Future of Hyrule]]" Scenario, Teba and Revali lead the Rito air force while Zelda leads all the ground forces as they rush to Hyrule Castle to take the fight to Astor and Harbinger Ganon. After both Harbinger Ganon and Astor are defeated, the latter enters into a full psychotic breakdown as he orders the former to destroy the heroes, before he himself gets absorbed by Ganon's Malice and some of it latches onto Terrako, possessing it as it unwillingly attacks Princess Zelda and Link. Once Terrako is sufficiently damaged to the point where it couldn't fight anymore, Teba and the warriors silently mourn its broken state as the now enraged princess swears to destroy Calamity Ganon once and for all and they charge for the sanctum where Ganon awaited them. However, because of his successful reincarnation, Ganon was impervious to all attacks so the princess, out of desperation, tried to use her power to seal the monster. Her power allowed Terrako to get back up and skitter upstairs to sacrifice itself to break down Ganon's defense, allowing the party to attack and eventually defeat him. With some cheering from Daruk and Revali,<ref name="AoC Daruk"/><ref name="AoC Revali 12"/> Link uses the Master Sword to critically weaken Ganon enough for Zelda to use her power to destroy him. With Hyrule reverting to its peaceful state, Terrako's blessed screw uses its power to send Teba, Sidon, Yunobo, and Riju back to the future. Teba and the other future counterparts soon depart from this timeline. As he fades away, Teba formally remarks that it was "enlightening," having been able to see "the face behind the Champion".<ref name="AoC Teba 10"/> as he was saying good-bye to Revali.<ref name="AoC Revali 13"/> After disappearing, Princess Zelda wishes them a brighter future.

In the secret Downloadable Content ending, Teba, Revali, and Tulin rest at the Flight Range. Tulin was sleeping on Revali's lap as the latter managed to keep the blanket from being blown away by the wind, as Teba chuckles happily at their bond with one another.

{{Heading|Gameplay}}
As a playable Warrior, Teba wields a [[Bow]] in a similar fashion to Revali, with the Falcon Bow being his default starting [[Weapon]]. Teba does not have a 'flying mode'; with certain attacks causing Teba to rise into the air. His attack style consists of a charge-and-release Arrow as his unique action. By pressing X repeatedly during any [[Strong Attack]], Teba unleashes a flurry of Arrows at [[Enemy|Enemies]], often zipping about as he does so.
{{Noncanon|End}}

==Trivia==
* Teba's design is based on a hawk.<ref name="CaC 129"/> He was originally intended to be brown, but in order to differentiate him from the other Rito, his coloration was changed to white.<ref name="CaC 129"/>

==Nomenclature==
Teba's name is derived from the Japanese 手羽 (''teba''), meaning "chicken wing". Teba and his wife [[Saki]]'s names are a pun on ''tebasaki'' (手羽先), a dish made of fried chicken wing tips.
{{Nomenclature}}

<ref name="BotW Teba 12">{{Cite|[Any pointers?] Using a bow in midair is just like using a bow on the ground. But you'll probably want a bow suited for long-range engagement.|Teba|BotW}}</ref>

<ref name="BotW Teba 16">{{Cite|[I've seen a few.] Don't be modest. I can tell just looking at you.|Teba|BotW}}</ref>
